## Overview

The script `03-near-completers-ttrain.R` utilizes student survey records from the `t_dacso_data_part_1` repository (DASCO survey data) along with administrative Student Transitions Project (STP) credential files to reclassify graduation status and identify a residual near-completer population. Individuals initially classified as non-graduates who subsequently attained provincial credentials or possessed prior administrative qualifications are flagged as "near-completers".

Frequency distributions and ratios of near-completers to completers are computed across several dimensions, resulting in three primary output tables: `t_dacso_near_completers_ratio_by_gender_year`, `t_dacso_near_completers_ratio_by_gender`, and `t_dacso_nearcompleters_ratioageatgradcip4`. These outputs provide both longitudinal and cross-sectional frequency counts, with ratios computed annually or averaged across representative reporting cycles—such as the 2018–2019 baseline utilized in the PSSM 2023 model—to ensure statistical stability. The final data products represent a purified synthesis of survey observations and longitudinal administrative evidence, enabling high-fidelity reporting of student outcomes across disparate academic fields.

## Methodology Overview

#### Demographic Attribute Normalization and Age Derivation

Student temporal markers are standardized by normalizing date formats and consolidating annual records into a longitudinal master repository. The student age at graduation is derived by comparing birth dates to administrative exit dates; these data are then joined to the primary dataset to facilitate the mandatory cohort eligibility filtering ($17 \le x \le 64$) required for provincial reporting.

#### Cohort Baseline and Longitudinal Analysis (Exploratory Only)

A unique subset of student records is used to establish a longitudinal baseline for cohort distribution analysis; the primary dataset is deduplicated and age-eligibility filters are applied ($17 \le x \le 64$). 

A frequency matrix that cross-tabulates graduation status against submission years is generated to **quantify** the statistical relationship between graduates and non-completers across multiple reporting cycles. These historical ratios help identify significant deviations in the data trend—such as the artificial variances introduced during the COVID-19 pandemic—and allow for the normalization of the cohort before final status reclassification.

#### Multi-Criteria Match Validation and Linkage

The primary relational linkage between survey respondents and provincial record systems is achieved using the Personal Education Number (PEN) as the unique identifier. This process integrates verified institutional credentials with the DACSO dataset and applies a standardized lookup to normalize program credential names for consistent reporting across the cohort.

Four primary criteria are used to validate that the provincial credential record aligns with the survey respondent's profile: 

* **Credential Type**
* **Program of Study (CIP code)**
* **Temporal Alignment (School Year)**
* **Institutional Identity**

A record is confirmed as a verified match if it satisfies **all four** criteria. Alternatively, if the specific 4-digit program code is missing but the high-level area of study (CIP-2) and the other three criteria match, the record is accepted to account for minor reporting variances in program classification.

#### Credential Promotion (Reclassification)

Verified records are partitioned into two discrete temporal windows based on the survey reporting cycle. Credentials awarded within or prior to the survey reporting cycle ($Year_{Award} \le Year_{Survey} + 1998$) are classified as "Before" awards, while those occurring subsequently are classified as "After" awards. This stratification ensures that the reclassification logic accounts for the timing of the award relative to the survey period.

A deterministic tie-breaking protocol is applied to students possessing multiple provincial credentials. The methodology prioritizes the most recent administrative record by selecting the credential with the maximum award year. In instances where multiple awards exist within the same award year, the record with the highest internal identifier ($ID$) is selected to ensure that each "Near-Completer" is reconciled against a singular, authoritative provincial record.

Finally, subjects originally classified as "Near-Completers" (Status 3) who possess a verified provincial credential are "promoted" to "Graduate" status (Status 1). This reclassification synthesizes survey-level observations with administrative data, producing the `grad_status_factoring_in_stp` attribute, which serves as the terminal variable for provincial longitudinal success reporting.

#### Age at Grad Ratios

The section outlines methodolgy originaly developed in this Excel workbook: _2017-2018\Development\Graduate Model\Near Completers_.
As such, this bolded sub-section labels include a reference to the associated column in the sheet _C\_Outc12\_13\_14RatiosAgeGradCIP4_ of the original workbook. Column references also indicate a section of code in the R script. Column references can be removed in the final draft.  If referencing the workbook as a guide, please note those values will not be identical to the 2023 outputs as different base years were used. 

##### Primary Baseline Consolidation (`base`)

A standardized baseline cohort is derived from the `t_dacso_data_part_1` administrative dataset consiting of records with the Outcomes 19 and 20 reporting cycles. Observations are stratified into discrete age cohorts via a non-equi join with the `age_group_lookup` table and synchronized with the `credential_rank` hierarchy. To ensure regulatory alignment, the cohort is restricted to institutional credentials verified for the PSSM 2017-18 framework. Taxonomic normalization is applied via regular expressions to purge administrative noise and deterministically reclassify credential prefixes from "1 - " to "3 - ".

##### Near Completers from Survey (Column H)

The "Near-Completer" population (`cosc_grad_status_lgds_cd_group = '3'`) is extracted from the consolidated baseline. A frequency matrix is generated by aggregating record counts across demographic age groups, 4-digit Classification of Instructional Programs (CIP) codes, and combined credential classifications.

##### Near Completers Changed to Graduate Status (Column I)

Records identified for status correction are isolated by filtering confirmed provincial matches (`has_stp_credential` = 'Yes'). These records are synchronized with the baseline cohort and aggregated by ademographic age groups, 4-digit Classification of Instructional Programs (CIP) codes, and combined credential classifications.  The final distributions quantify individuals whose academic status was transitioned from "Near-Completer" to "Graduate" based on external Student Transitions Project (STP) evidence.

##### Confirmed Graduate from STP (Column K)

Recordss are identified for individuals attaining a confirmed graduate status factoring in administrative promotion (`grad_status_factoring_in_stp` = '1'). The cohort is restricted to the 17–64 age range aggregated by ademographic age groups, 4-digit Classification of Instructional Programs (CIP) codes, and combined credential classifications to provide count of total graduates.

##### Confirmed Completers from Survey (Column M)

Baseline graduate records are isolated for survey-reported graduates (`cosc_grad_status_lgds_cd_group` = '1') within the 17–64 age parameter. Counts are aggregated by demographic age groups, 4-digit Classification of Instructional Programs (CIP) codes, and combined credential classifications.  The distributions represent the quantity of completers prior to the application of administrative promotion logic.

##### Final Age at Grad Ratios

The final analytical phase implements a multivariate join of the four preceding distributions. The residual Near-Completer population is derived through the following subtraction:

$$NC_{Residual} = NC_{Survey} - NC_{Promoted}$$

Final ratios are established by dividing the residual population by total graduate counts, both factoring and not factoring external administrative evidence:

$$Ratio_{Baseline} = \frac{NC_{Residual}}{Completers_{Survey}}$$
$$Ratio = \frac{NC_{Residual}}{Completers_{Survey+STP}}$$


Calculated values resulting in mathematical infinity are recoded as `NA` to ensure the statistical integrity of the final report.

#### Gender at Grad Ratios

As with Age Ratios, this section outlines methodolgy originaly developed in this Excel workbook: _2017-2018\Development\Graduate Model\Near Completers_. Bolded sub-section labels include a reference to the associated column in sheet _C\_Outc12\_13\_14RatiosByGender_ of the original workbook.

##### Primary Baseline Consolidation (`base`)
A standardized baseline cohort is derived from the `t_dacso_data_part_1` dataset for Outcomes 19 and 20. Observations are restricted to respondents with valid gender identifiers (`tpid_lgnd_cd != '0'`) and are stratified into discrete age cohorts via a non-equi join with the `age_group_lookup` table. The resulting dataset is synchronized with the `credential_rank` hierarchy to ensure institutional program names are linked to recognized categorical metadata.

##### Near Completers from Survey (Column E)
The "Near-Completer" population (`cosc_grad_status_lgds_cd_group` = '3') is extracted from the consolidated baseline. A frequency matrix is generated that aggregates respondent counts by gender identifier, demographic age group, and institutional program credential. 

##### Near Completers Changed to Graduate Status (Column F)
Records requiring status correction are identified by synchronizing the baseline with the `t_dacso_data_part_1_tempselection` metadata. The cohort is filtered for confirmed provincial matches (`has_stp_credential` = 'Yes'). The final distributions quantify individuals whose academic status was transitioned from "Near-Completer" to "Graduate" based on external Student Transitions Project (STP) evidence.

##### Confirmed Completers from Survey (Column H)
Baseline graduate records (`cosc_grad_status_lgds_cd_group` = '1') are isolated from the baseline. Observations are restricted to the 17–64 age range and aggregated by gender, age cohort, and institutional credential. This frequency distribution represents a count of survey-confirmed graduates prior to administrative adjustments.

##### Final Gender-Specific Success Ratios
The final analytical phase implements a multivariate join of the three preceding distributions. The residual Near-Completer population (`n_nc_stp`) is derived through a deterministic subtraction:

$$NC_{Residual} = NC_{Survey} - NC_{Promoted}$$

Terminal success ratios are established by dividing the residual Near-Completer population by the total confirmed survey graduates:

$$Ratio_{Baseline} = \frac{NC_{Residual}}{Completers_{Survey}}$$

Calculated values are subjected to data cleaning where numeric missingness is replaced with zero to ensure the statistical integrity of the final provincial success ratio reporting.

#### Gender at Grad Ratios by Year

A longitudinal variant of the Gender at Grad Ratios modifies the baseline aggregation logic by adding submission cycle identifier (`coci_subm_cd`) to the list of grouping varibales for all frequency tables. Unlike the aggregate model, this methodology maintains discrete record sets for each reporting period. This technical adjustment allows the reporting framework to generate independent success ratios for each cycle, providing a high-fidelity view of institutional performance trends over time.

## Key Output Tables

The following data objects represent the terminal outputs of the near-completer stratification and ratio calculation pipeline. These tables are taxonomically aligned with the PSSM 2017-18 framework and incorporate longitudinal administrative adjustments.

##### t_dacso_nearcompleters_ratioageatgradcip4

Success ratios stratified by age-group, 4-digit Classification of Instructional Programs (CIP-4) and normalized credential categories.

<ul class="list-variable-names">
  <li>age_group (string): The categorical age cohort.</li>
  <li>lcip4_cred (string): The taxonomically normalized program and credential identifier, subjected to regex-based cleaning.</li>
  <li>lcp4_cd (string): The primary 4-digit CIP classification code.</li>
  <li>count (numeric): The frequency of survey-reported Near-Completers.</li>
  <li>nc_with_earlier_or_later (numeric): The count of individuals promoted via provincial administrative verification.</li>
  <li>completers (numeric): The total graduate count factoring in administrative adjustments.</li>
  <li>c_not_factoring_stp (numeric): The baseline graduate count derived exclusively from survey reporting.</li>
  <li>near_completers_stp_cred (numeric): The net residual Near-Completer count.</li>
  <li>ratio (numeric): The primary success ratio utilizing STP-adjusted graduate counts.</li>
  <li>ratio_not_factoring_stp (numeric): The baseline success ratio utilizing survey-only graduate counts.</li>
</ul>

##### t_dacso_near_completers_ratio_by_gender

Success ratios across the multi-year reporting period, providing a cumulative assessment of provincial performance.

<ul class="list-variable-names">
  <li>gender (numeric): Numeric standardized gender identifier.</li>
  <li>age_group (string): The categorical age cohort.</li>
  <li>prgm_credential_awarded_name (string): The institutional nomenclature for the awarded credential.</li>
  <li>count (numeric): The cumulative frequency of survey-reported Near-Completers.</li>
  <li>nc_with_early_or_late (numeric): The cumulative count of administratively promoted graduates across all reporting cycles.</li>
  <li>completers (numeric): The cumulative count of survey-confirmed graduates.</li>
  <li>n_nc_stp (numeric): The net residual Near-Completer population within the aggregate cohort.</li>
  <li>ratio (numeric): The aggregate success ratio representing the cumulative multi-year period.</li>
</ul>

##### t_dacso_near_completers_ratio_by_gender_year
A longitudinal frequency distribution of success ratios, disaggregated by individual submission cycles and demographic indicators.

<ul class="list-variable-names">
  <li>coci_subm_cd (string): The administrative submission cycle identifier (e.g., "C_Outc20").</li>
  <li>gender (numeric): Numeric standardized gender identifier derived from the primary survey records.</li>
  <li>age_group (string): The categorical age cohort mapped via the non-equi join protocol.</li>
  <li>prgm_credential_awarded_name (string): The institutional nomenclature for the awarded credential.</li>
  <li>count (numeric): The frequency of respondents maintaining a survey-reported "Near-Completer" status.</li>
  <li>nc_with_early_or_late (numeric): The frequency of individuals promoted to "Graduate" status via administrative Student Transitions Project (STP) evidence.</li>
  <li>completers (numeric): The count of survey-confirmed graduates within the specified strata.</li>
  <li>n_nc_stp (numeric): The net residual Near-Completer count following deterministic administrative adjustments.</li>
  <li>ratio (numeric): The calculated success ratio, defined as the quotient of the residual population and confirmed graduates.</li>
  <li>year (numeric): The calendar year corresponding to the submission cycle (e.g., 2019).</li>
</ul>
